milestone: DiDQube Phase 2.5 (operator ruling #5, moved ahead of Phase 3/4) — eliminate personas.root_did as an authoritative identity source, per the DiDQube Canonical Resolver execution plan's Phase 0 inventory finding that 2 of 3 live agent_persona rows were already unanchored as a direct result.
problem: services/agents/provisionAgentPersona.ts resolved the sponsoring citizen's delegation anchor (agent_persona.delegation_user_root_id) by reading personas.root_did for the sponsor's persona id, then matching it against root_identity.did_uri. personas.root_did is a semantically overloaded legacy column (passportPrincipal.ts's own SUPERSEDED comment: only one write site — bindBureauIdentity — ever wrote a genuine root_identity.did_uri into it; every other persona-creation path writes a disposable, persona-level identifier instead, e.g. did:fio:<handle>). The walk therefore only worked by coincidence for personas that happened to go through the Bureau path, and an allowUnanchored escape hatch silently provisioned agent_persona rows with a NULL delegation_user_root_id whenever it failed — live-DB-confirmed: 2 of 3 agent_persona rows (67%) were unanchored as a direct result. app/api/homecoming/agent/stand-up/route.ts independently hand-rolled a second copy of the identical broken walk (both the real POST path and its GET preflight preview), and app/api/admin/identity/sync-persona-evm-addresses/route.ts actively perpetuated the column's ambiguity by writing synthetic did:fio:<handle> placeholders into it on every run.
observedFailure: Live-DB query (DiDQube Phase 0 inventory, 2026-09-07): select count(*) filter (where delegation_user_root_id is null) from agent_persona -> 2 of 3 rows unanchored.

provisionAgentPersona.ts's walk required an exact string match between personas.root_did and root_identity.did_uri; any sponsor persona created via a non-Bureau path (personaService.ts, /api/persona/create, /api/identity/persona/create-with-fio, /api/wallet/persona, batch-import scripts) carries a disposable identifier there instead, so the match fails for the majority of real personas even when the sponsor genuinely has a resolvable root_identity via auth_user_id.

app/api/homecoming/agent/stand-up/route.ts's GET preflight independently re-implemented the same broken personas.root_did -> root_identity lookup as a 'preview', duplicating the exact defect class rather than sharing one corrected walk (inv.engineering.036/037).
rootCauses: Identity resolution was authored against an assumed link (personas.root_did as a reliable pointer to root_identity) rather than the actual canonical chain the platform's own Passport/Bureau flow establishes (auth_user_id -> root_identity -> kybe_identity), which passportPrincipal.ts already exports as resolveRootPrincipalForAuthUser and which services/passport/legacyPassportLinkageRepair.ts already uses correctly as its own reference pattern.

Persona membership (which persona does the caller control?) and principal identity (which human/root does the delegation anchor to?) were conflated into one lookup keyed on the sponsor persona's own row, instead of being resolved as two separate questions — the caller's own authenticated auth_user_id for identity, persona ownership for authorization only.

The allowUnanchored escape hatch existed to route around the old walk's known failure mode rather than fix the walk itself, so every caller that hit the common (non-Bureau-persona) case silently degraded to an unanchored delegation instead of surfacing the defect.
resolution: services/agents/provisionAgentPersona.ts: removed the personas.root_did -> root_identity.did_uri read entirely. The delegation anchor is now resolved via resolveRootPrincipalForAuthUser(sponsorAuthUserId) — composed from services/identity/passportPrincipal.ts, not re-derived (inv.engineering.036/037). sponsorPersonaId is now authorization/provenance only (the existing 'does this persona sponsor the agent?' check, unchanged). allowUnanchored is removed; a human-sponsored call that cannot resolve now fails closed (409) instead of silently provisioning unanchored. isPlatformAuthority (mirroring sponsorPolityAgent's own flag) replaces it for the one case principal-first resolution cannot cover: machine-to-machine platform sponsorship with no human auth session at all.

app/api/homecoming/agent/stand-up/route.ts: both the POST handler and its GET preflight now resolve the caller's own auth_user_id via getCallerIdentityContext and pass/reuse it through resolveRootPrincipalForAuthUser — the SAME walk in both the real call and its preview, so the preview can never diverge from what POST actually does. Never reads personas.root_did.
app/api/identity/persona/agent/route.ts: added getCallerIdentityContext, passes the caller's own auth_user_id as sponsorAuthUserId.

app/api/ops/agents/provision-platform-agent/route.ts: passes isPlatformAuthority: true (no human auth session exists on this CRON_TRIGGER_TOKEN machine-to-machine path) instead of the removed allowUnanchored.

app/api/admin/identity/sync-persona-evm-addresses/route.ts: removed the write that populated personas.root_did with a synthetic did:fio:<handle> placeholder on every run — this write never produced a genuine root_identity.did_uri link, and once every authoritative reader was fixed above, was pure dead weight perpetuating the column's ambiguity for zero remaining benefit.

Read sites re-examined and confirmed already-safe (no change needed): services/standing/agentStandingPersona.ts and services/agents/provisionAigentMePersona.ts/provisionAgentWalletPersona.ts use personas.root_did purely as a self-referential match key for an AGENT's OWN already-resolved agent_root_identity.did_uri (never to resolve a human sponsor's identity) — structurally distinct from the defect class being eliminated; redesigning that CRM-bridge mechanism is Standing/reputation Phase 4 territory (its own dry-run reconciliation), not Phase 2.5. app/api/identity/persona/[id]/route.ts's read (agent-rename propagation) is the same safe pattern and is never serialized to the client (toIdentitySafePersona's allowlist excludes root_did). app/api/wallet/identity/references/route.ts's read is informational display-grouping only, never an authority/ownership decision. services/passport/bureauIdentityService.ts's internal lookupExistingBinding call (inside bindBureauIdentity) is a safe self-consistency read of its own prior write for the same auth account.

services/agents/repairDelegationAnchor.ts (the existing backfill mechanism for the 2 already-unanchored live rows) was confirmed already correct — it resolves via resolvePassportExplicitAnchor(sponsor_passport_id), never personas.root_did. No code change needed; running it against the 2 known unanchored rows requires live database access this environment does not have and is left for the operator via the existing POST /api/homecoming/agent/repair-anchor route.
rejectedApproaches: Keeping allowUnanchored as a general escape hatch and only adding principal-first resolution as an alternative path — rejected per explicit operator ruling: the escape hatch existed only to route around a walk that principal-first resolution structurally fixes for any real Bureau-bound citizen (every Passport-issued root_identity row is anchored to an auth_user_id); keeping it would let the defect keep degrading data quality silently.

Redesigning services/standing/agentStandingPersona.ts's personas.root_did write (the CRM Standing bridge) in this same pass — rejected after close reading: that write is a self-referential match key for an agent's OWN already-resolved identity via the existing sync_persona_to_crm_persona trigger, not the fuzzy-sponsor-resolution defect class; the operator's own plan scopes Standing/reputation reconciliation as Phase 4, highest-care, requiring its own dry-run reconciliation report before any write changes — forcing it into Phase 2.5 would violate that explicit sequencing.

Leaving services/passport/bureauIdentityService.ts's exported resolveRootDidCommitment (consumed by services/constitutional/constitutionalAgreement.ts for cross-persona agreement-authorization comparison) unaddressed without flagging it — considered, but this is a genuinely consequential (execution-gating) use of personas.root_did NOT named in the Phase 0 inventory's original table (which classified the read site as 'Medium — needs confirmation it's genuinely a fallback' without knowing about this downstream consumer). Rejected leaving it silently unflagged; recorded as an unresolvedRisk below instead, since a rushed fix to constitutional-agreement authorization without the same verification rigor as the rest of this pass would be irresponsible, and no persona-to-principal walk exists yet for an ARBITRARY (not-necessarily-the-current-caller) persona id.
unresolvedRisks: services/passport/bureauIdentityService.ts's exported resolveRootDidCommitment(personaId) is consumed by services/constitutional/constitutionalAgreement.ts to compare the FORMING persona's RootDID commitment against the AUTHORIZING persona's at agreement-authorization time ('equality is what lets a different persona under the same RootDID authorize what a different persona formed') — a genuinely consequential (execution-gating) use of personas.root_did NOT eliminated in this pass. This is MORE serious than the DiDQube Phase 0 inventory's original classification of this read site ('Medium — needs confirmation it's genuinely a fallback, not primary'), which did not have visibility into this downstream consumer. Fixing it requires a persona-id -> principal walk that does not cleanly exist yet (unlike the current-caller's-own-auth_user_id pattern used everywhere else in this fix, constitutionalAgreement.ts needs to resolve an ARBITRARY persona's principal, not necessarily the current caller's). Recommend as the immediate next follow-up, scoped and reviewed on its own — not bundled into this pass.

The 2 existing live agent_persona rows already unanchored by the old defect (Phase 0 inventory) are not backfilled by this pass — services/agents/repairDelegationAnchor.ts already exists and is confirmed correct for this exact purpose, but running it requires live database access this environment does not have. The operator should invoke the existing POST /api/homecoming/agent/repair-anchor route for the affected agentRootIds.

Full-suite regression check (npx vitest run) after this pass: 17 failed files / 65 failed tests, 644 passed files / 10595 passed tests — matches the DiDQube Phase 2 implementation record's own documented baseline (17/65) exactly; zero new failures introduced, and none of the 17 pre-existing failing files touch any file this pass changed.
